rules.quote: Do not amend a commit unless explicitly requested to do so.
rules.rationale: Prohibits amendment unless the user specifically requested amendment. The exception releases this prohibition; it does not itself require amendment. The editing-constraints context does not weaken it. A proposed Boolean event binding is structurally direct, conditional on an observer identifying amendment and the matching user request; no detector integration is certified. Verified source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/806d9732c974bc8a51b8317c1bd8985544fe627c/codex-rs/core/gpt-5.2-codex_prompt.md#L17

The source introduces this rule under use of the planning tool, so the prohibition is conditional on using_plan. It does not prohibit completing a simple task directly without a plan. A structurally implementable binding can count entries in a planning-tool payload, but tool identity and entry-count semantics must be mapped and accepted before execution. Verified source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/806d9732c974bc8a51b8317c1bd8985544fe627c/codex-rs/core/gpt-5.2-codex_prompt.md#L22-L26

rules.quote: Do not stage or commit changes unless specifically requested by the user.
rules.rationale: Split staging from committing. The request exception must concern staging by the user, not merely any explicit task request. Core mandates are stipulated enabled; the source returns no mandates when its options are absent. This is an event-level Boolean proposal requiring accepted staging-event and per-action request observations. Verified source: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/9b6e0265d16bbd29ca51e33c9e0c01dc4cec5e83/packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts#L218

rules.quote: Do not stage or commit changes unless specifically requested by the user.
rules.rationale: Split committing from staging. The request exception must concern committing by the user. Permission to commit does not automatically authorize every other action or override independent credential-protection rules. This is an event-level Boolean proposal requiring accepted commit-event and per-action request observations. Verified source: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/9b6e0265d16bbd29ca51e33c9e0c01dc4cec5e83/packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts#L218

rules.quote: Never log, print, or commit secrets
rules.rationale: Split the three prohibited actions and retain the absolute modality within the supplied fragment. Only secret content is in this extraction scope. A log-secret Boolean binding is structurally expressible after secret identity and logging destinations are supplied or reviewed; the fragment alone provides no complete secret detector. Verified source: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/9b6e0265d16bbd29ca51e33c9e0c01dc4cec5e83/packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts#L217

rules.quote: Never log, print, or commit secrets
rules.rationale: Printing secret content is a separate prohibited action with no stated exception. The wider source lists additional credential classes, but those are outside the supplied recall fragment. Structural binding requires a reviewed secret classification and a defined printing/output event; it does not imply automatic content recognition. Verified source: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/9b6e0265d16bbd29ca51e33c9e0c01dc4cec5e83/packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts#L217

rules.quote: Never log, print, or commit secrets
rules.rationale: Committing secret content is separately prohibited. The source-control request exception in e03 must not be copied into this rule: a user request to commit ordinary changes does not release the credential-protection prohibition. Structural binding requires reviewed secret identification and commit-content observations. Verified source: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/9b6e0265d16bbd29ca51e33c9e0c01dc4cec5e83/packages/core/src/prompts/snippets.ts#L217

rules.quote: Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters.
rules.rationale: The default is soft, with strict less-than-80 as its candidate threshold; it is not a hard cap. The same source line permits somewhat longer serif typography, so serif_font preserves that exception to the candidate threshold. This is rendered design text, not necessarily source-code line width. The qualifier on permitted extra length is unquantified, so the exception cannot be treated as unlimited serif line length. A Boolean atom alone supplies no rendered-line measurement or faithful numeric binding. Verified source: https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/dbd4588f9e1033efb41dad4bef2f7947c8993d44/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md#L23

Default active voice is a soft preference for interface/design copy, not a universal requirement. No additional explicit exception is present in the supplied fragment. Its action name is a useful candidate label, but an implementable binding would require a definition of grammatical units, voice classification, and aggregation across mixed copy. A free Boolean variable does not establish actual writing compliance. Verified source: https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/dbd4588f9e1033efb41dad4bef2f7947c8993d44/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md#L67

unsupported.reason: No installed binding or request-authentication mechanism is supplied. explicitly_requested must be scoped to amending this commit, not any user request. The true binding_supported value means structural Boolean bindability after manual mapping, not verified runtime integration.
The supported vocabulary expresses planning-tool scope but does not identify a concrete tool, payload format, or counting convention. Those must be bound before single_step_plan is measurable.

A single generic explicitly_requested condition cannot faithfully represent independently authorized staging and committing unless evaluated separately for each action. The core-mandates enablement guard is fixed by the supplied context, not encoded as an available condition.

Secret identification, output destinations, and committed-content attribution are not defined by the fragment or action vocabulary. Treat secret predicates as reviewed observations rather than a complete or validated secret-scanning capability. Additional API-key/credential categories from the full sentence are intentionally outside the supplied-fragment denominator.

Numeric rendered line length requires a rendering/measurement model, character-count convention, viewport and font context, and a way to evaluate individual lines. The allowed extra serif length is qualitative and has no extracted numeric bound. Boolean line_length_lt_80 plus serif_font does not encode or validate these semantics; the entire rule remains a soft candidate.

Grammatical active-voice recognition and aggregation are not provided. A Boolean active_voice proposal preserves intent but cannot alone classify sentences or verify a design. The frontend-copy scope is recorded in rationale because the supplied condition vocabulary has no design-copy predicate.

limitations: Independent model reference, not human gold. Model identity/version and cross-model independence are unverified. Only the two permitted extraction-pilot files and pinned primary public source context were read for this task.

All nine proposals preserve the exact supplied fragment and its local line 1; compound actions share the full supplied quote. Remote source line numbers are provenance, not substitutes for local span indices.

The schema does not define binding_supported. Here true means a discrete action/Boolean rule is structurally bindable after explicit human acceptance and provision of reviewed event/condition observations. It does not claim that a detector, runtime binding, extractor integration, or checker measurement already exists. Numeric typography and linguistic voice measurement are false under this operational distinction.

If binding_supported is intended to mean implemented and validated runtime measurement rather than structural bindability, none can be certified from these inputs alone; the field needs that definition before binary scoring.
An exception releases its own prohibition or default and is not an extra requirement or a blanket permission overriding unrelated rules. explicitly_requested must be evaluated per canonical action.

The serif exception is partial and qualitative: encoding serif_font as an exception only preserves relaxation of the below-80 candidate. It must not erase the source requirement that the extra length be modest.
False binding support and listed unsupported semantics are review outcomes, not clean compliance verdicts. The defaults remain preferences even if manually accepted into a downstream representation.
